tools.name: publish_site
tools.description: Use this when the user wants something put online, shared as a link, or hosted. Publishes files to a live permanent URL at the chosen slug. Returns {url, slug, version, token?}. The token appears only on the first anonymous publish; store it to update later.

tools.name: update_site
tools.description: Use this to replace (or with merge=true, add to) the files of a slug you already own. Requires the token from the first publish. Returns the same shape as publish_site with a bumped version.

tools.name: get_site
tools.description: Use this to check whether a slug is live and read its URL, version, size, and timestamps. Public; no token needed.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: Use this to list every live site owned by your token, with URLs and versions.

tools.name: delete_site
tools.description: Use this only when the user explicitly asks to take a site down. Permanently removes the slug you own; the slug becomes free.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Use this to read your plan, limits, and how many sites your token owns.

tools.name: get_upgrade_link
tools.description: Use this only when the user asks for higher limits. Returns a Stripe Checkout URL for Hobby ($3/mo) or Pro ($15/mo) tied to your token. A human must open it and pay; nothing is charged by this call.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_site, list_sites, get_upgrade_link · Private data: publish_site, update_site, get_site, list_sites, whoami, get_upgrade_link · Public sink: publish_site, update_site · Destructive: delete_site.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_site, list_sites, get_upgrade_link · Private data: publish_site, update_site, get_site, list_sites, whoami, get_upgrade_link · Public sink: publish_site, update_site · Destructive: delete_site

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
